bull_bear.body: Balance sheet is deliberately clean post-IPO: **INR 1,639 cr of cash** including INR 689 cr of IPO proceeds, **long-term debt fully repaid in April 2026**, DSO improved to 71 days (54 billed), cash conversion to EBITDA ~70%, ROCE ~13%. Forward cover is taken only as a cash-flow hedge. Capital deployment priorities visible on the call: R&D into platforms (gated), senior leadership hiring, and continued funding of the Qure.ai associate position. No buyback, dividend or acquisition was discussed.
bull_bear.title: Capital allocation

bull_bear.body:
- **TMT concentration risk realised.** A −22% YoY decline in one vertical cut group growth from 37% to 20%. The stated cause is structural, not idiosyncratic: big tech's AI capex "almost doubled," creating opex pressure and "big adjustments… in terms of how they look at the overall spends and allocating more of that to capex and less of that to opex." That pressure does not obviously reverse in a quarter.
- **The company has stopped disclosing client-specific issues** — "we have chosen to not talk about that in future because it is distracting." This reduces transparency exactly where the volatility is.
- **Currency dependence:** 11 of the 20 points of reported growth. cc revenue was *down* 0.4% sequentially.
- **CFO transition** at a moment when the equity story depends on financial credibility; successor unnamed.
- **AI work compression** — "anything that feels like it is not as relevant today… could be completely vanishing" (ad hoc analysis, dashboards "going to zero"). Management argues the expanding pie more than compensates, but the compression is certain and the compensation is a forecast.
- **Competitive intensity rising:** "there are also many players who want a piece of this pie right now… our execution has to really get better."
- Asper revenue flat despite 59% ARR growth — the recognition lag has to actually close in H2.
bull_bear.title: Risks & watch-items

bull_bear.body: Unusually accountable. The CEO refused to blame the TMT client — "I do not want to get into blaming anyone for our performance… I will take most of the blame on our own execution" — and repeatedly framed the shortfall as internal: "It is completely left to our execution to become as big as we can be. There is no other law of gravity applying to us." He conceded outright that "our quarter one is not as great as we would like it to be" and that Q1 "underachieved." Disclosure is improving voluntarily — committing to publish Cogentiq and license revenue from next quarter, and considering disclosing partnership-led revenue. The CFO gave precise bridges (currency vs merit vs headcount in gross margin; the exact Q2 merit impact) and corrected an analyst's mischaracterisation of the segment loss as a one-time integration cost. The one weakening of transparency is the deliberate policy to stop discussing client-specific issues.
bull_bear.title: Management quality / tone

bull_bear.body:
- **The reported 20% growth is really 9%.** Constant-currency revenue *fell* 0.4% sequentially. Every profitability metric is genuine; the top line is substantially FX.
- **The >INR 20 mn client count went 6 → 5 sequentially** even though it is up YoY (4 → 5) — a TMT client slipped below the threshold. Management guided investors to look at this annually, not on a TTM basis, which is a fair methodological point but also softens a negative datapoint.
- **The Fractal Alpha loss widening from INR 4 cr to INR 14 cr is an accounting relocation, not deterioration** — iqigai and EdTech investment simply moved segments, with FY26 restated. Reading it as operational decay is wrong.
- **AI deflation is being embraced as an expansion argument:** work that took a year may take a month, "which means that per se looks like it shrunk, but there are now 1,000 such deals rather than 10 such deals earlier." This is the central, unproven bet of the entire business model.
- Fractal is becoming a **partner-mediated** business — five of its largest deals came via Databricks/OpenAI/Anthropic — which is a new dependency it did not previously carry ("Most of our revenues used to come from direct client relationships").
- Qure.ai's backlog going from ~INR 20 cr to INR 100+ cr is arguably the largest forward-looking datapoint on the call, and it sits in an associate line most models treat as noise.

bull_bear.body:

bull_bear.title: Bull — competitive strengths

bull_bear.body:
- Client concentration — The Board's report flags "client concentration" among the risks and uncertainties attached to its forward-looking statements, and discloses that in FY 2025-26 the Company worked with 104 MWC clients "which contributed to 81.6% of Fractal.ai revenue" — so a large share of the segment's revenue rests on a narrow set of enterprise relationships.
- Talent scarcity and wage inflation — The cautionary statement names "wage increases in India" and "our ability to attract and retain highly skilled professionals" as risk factors; in a people-led AI services model, attrition or salary escalation feeds straight into delivery cost and margin.
- Intense competition and erosion of cost advantage — The cautionary statement names "intense competition in IT business, including those factors, that may affect our cost advantage" — pricing pressure from both traditional IT services incumbents and newer AI entrants is a structural feature of the market.
- Geographic concentration and cross-border delivery / immigration restrictions — The cautionary statement names "restrictions on immigration", "our ability to manage our international operations" and "political instability"; the Board's report records Fractal.ai revenue as "67.3% from Americas, 19.9% from Europe & 12.8% from APAC & Others", and the double-materiality assessment lists "Trade Restrictions and Cross Border Delivery" as a material topic.
- Demand cyclicality in key focus verticals — The cautionary statement names "reduced demand for technology in our key focus areas" and "general economic conditions affecting our industry" — enterprise technology budgets in CPGR, TMT, HLS and BFSI can be deferred in a downturn.
- Contract execution risk on fixed-price engagements — The cautionary statement names "time and cost overruns on fixed-price, fixed-time frame contracts" and "liability for damages on our service contracts" — cost overrun on a fixed-price statement of work is absorbed by the Company, not the client.
- Acquisition and integration risk — The cautionary statement names "our ability to complete and integrate potential acquisitions" — the group already runs a wide subsidiary structure, so integration failure is a recurring exposure.
- Intellectual property, data privacy and cyber security — The cautionary statement names "unauthorized use of our intellectual property"; "Data Privacy and Cyber Security" and "Responsible AI" also appear among the material topics identified in the ESRS-aligned double materiality assessment — client data handling and model governance are core to the service proposition.
- Service delivery continuity and operational resilience — The cautionary statement names "disruptions in telecommunication networks"; "Service Delivery Continuity & Operational Resilience" is listed as a material topic in the double materiality assessment. The Board's report also notes internal audit reviews of controls and risks in "software delivery, accounting and finance, procurement, employee engagement, travel, insurance, IT processes".
- Withdrawal of governmental fiscal incentives — The cautionary statement names "withdrawal of Governmental fiscal incentives" among the risk factors — a tax/incentive change would flow directly to the reported tax charge and cash flow.

latest_quarter.body: Gross margin expanded only 29 bps to 45.7% — a currency gain of 273 bps was almost entirely consumed by the merit increase (−75 bps) and a deliberate headcount build to support future growth (−169 bps). The real operating leverage is in SG&A, down from 26.2% to 24.3% of revenue, delivering the 189 bps adjusted EBITDA expansion. **Q2 carries a 120-130 bps P&L headwind** from three full months of merit increases versus one in Q1. ESOP charges including cash bonus and one-time retention fell to 1.2% of revenue from 1.4%. The margin philosophy is explicitly disciplined: R&D rises only as a share of *expanded* gross margin, enforced by a formal system, and the CEO is pushing R&D itself to "work backwards from revenue" for faster conversion. The mix shift toward outcome/output/license pricing (42% → target 60%) is the structural margin lever.

outlook.body: Fractal is an asset-light enterprise AI business, so its expansion narrative is about platform, capability, vertical and geographic build-out rather than plant or capacity addition. Coming into FY27 the company has consolidated its offering into three pillars on one platform with one go-to-market — AI-led Transformation (AIT), AI Foundations (AIF) and AI Work & Workforce (AIW) — all powered by Cogentiq, its flagship agentic AI platform, and delivered through integrated business units organized by industry (CPGR, FSI, HLS, TMT) and by the APAC and Europe geographies. Cogentiq adoption is described as transitioning from POC to production deployment, with platform revenue expected to accelerate and drive further margin expansion in FY27. Capability build-out is funded by R&D: 6.4% of revenue was invested in R&D across the two segments in FY 2025-26, of which 4.1% was expensed and the balance capitalized on the back of intellectual property developed. Vertical and geographic expansion is evidenced by Healthcare & Life Sciences rising from 13.8% to 19.3% of revenue and Europe from 17.7% to 19.9%. Inorganic expansion is framed as optionality rather than a committed project: a strong cash position (stated as C20.5 billion) is said to enable disciplined inorganic growth through M&A to acquire complementary capabilities, verticals or geographies, while retaining flexibility for organic investment in R&D, talent and infrastructure. No named capex project, commissioning date or capacity addition is disclosed.

outlook.body:
- Revenue expansion within existing clients — net revenue retention of 117% in the Fractal.ai segment in FY 2025-26, measured including upsells, cross-sells and contractions.
- Deepening penetration of large enterprise accounts — 104 MWC clients contributing 81.6% of Fractal.ai revenue.
- Product-led growth from Fractal Alpha, which contributed C 908 million of revenue with 41% growth year-on-year.
- Geographic mix weighted to the Americas (67.3% of Fractal.ai revenue), with Europe at 19.9% and APAC & Others at 12.8%.
- Client advocacy as a retention and acquisition lever — Net Promoter Score of 78 for FY 2025-26.
- R&D-created intellectual property as the source of reusable, productized delivery — part of the 6.4% of revenue spent on R&D is capitalized on the back of IP developed.
- Client demand pattern evidenced in the case studies: enterprises buying agentic AI platforms to compress decision cycles (HCP query response from 3-4 days to seconds; over 75% reduction in time-to-insight; ~4x faster data pipeline build) and to close AI capability gaps in their own workforces.
- A deployed agentic platform for a pharmaceutical client is "live in production across initial brands, with additional brands and markets in the onboarding pipeline" — a qualitative expansion pipeline within an existing account, not a disclosed order book.
- A workforce-transformation program for a US healthcare payer "expanded further following initial success", indicating follow-on scope within the account.

deepdive.thesis: Profitability is compounding faster than revenue and management is openly unhappy with the revenue line: net income +92% YoY to INR 72 cr, adjusted EBITDA margin 16.8% (+189 bps) on revenue of INR 912.5 cr (+20% reported, **only +9% constant currency**) — because a single vertical, TMT, declined 22% YoY and dragged group growth from 37% ex-TMT down to 20%. Underlying client health is excellent (NRR 117%, NPS 77, zero churn, top-10 concentration down to 51.8%), and the CEO's diagnosis is blunt and self-directed: "It is completely left to our execution." TMT is called bottomed with sequential growth expected in Q2. CFO Ashwath Bhat departs; successor process is advanced but unannounced.

risks.note: The Board's report flags "client concentration" among the risks and uncertainties attached to its forward-looking statements, and discloses that in FY 2025-26 the Company worked with 104 MWC clients "which contributed to 81.6% of Fractal.ai revenue" — so a large share of the segment's revenue rests on a narrow set of enterprise relationships.

The cautionary statement names "wage increases in India" and "our ability to attract and retain highly skilled professionals" as risk factors; in a people-led AI services model, attrition or salary escalation feeds straight into delivery cost and margin.

The cautionary statement names "intense competition in IT business, including those factors, that may affect our cost advantage" — pricing pressure from both traditional IT services incumbents and newer AI entrants is a structural feature of the market.

one-line thesis: Profitability is compounding faster than revenue and management is openly unhappy with the revenue line: net income +92% YoY to INR 72 cr, adjusted EBITDA margin 16.8% (+189 bps) on revenue of INR 912.5 cr (+20% reported, **only +9% constant currency**) — because a single vertical, TMT, declined 22% YoY and dragged group growth from 37% ex-TMT down to 20%. Underlying client health is excellent (NRR 117%, NPS 77, zero churn, top-10 concentration down to 51.8%), and the CEO's diagnosis is blunt and self-directed: "It is completely left to our execution." TMT is called bottomed with sequential growth expected in Q2. CFO Ashwath Bhat departs; successor process is advanced but unannounced.

> **Adjustments / one-offs:** the 20% reported growth is **11 points of currency** — cc growth was 9% YoY and *negative* 0.4% QoQ. Merit increases were made effective **1 June** (unusually — normally 1 April), so only **one month** hit Q1; the full three-month impact lands in Q2 and is quantified at **120-130 bps at the P&L level** (75 bps of it in gross margin). The Fractal Alpha segment loss widened from INR 4 cr to **INR 14 cr** *not* from deterioration but from a **restatement**: iqigai and EdTech teams were moved from Fractal.ai into Analytics Vidhya, with FY26 segment numbers restated. Qure.ai contributed a **INR 23 cr share of loss** (vs INR 22 cr) even though its revenue grew 160% YoY to INR 24 cr. Management flagged that "our profitability in the first quarter is always a little lower than the following quarters" — sequential comparison is not meaningful.
guidance (critical — verify next quarter:
- **TMT: "healthy sequential growth in TMT the next quarter"** — the single most checkable commitment on the call. Visibility comes from **new deals with existing clients already "in the bag"**, not new logos.
- **Outcome/output/license revenue mix: 42% today → "we want to get it to 60 over the next few quarters."**
- **R&D to rise toward 10% of revenue**, but strictly gated — "we will do it only on the back of expanded margins… only expanded gross margins, a part of that will flow through to higher R&D spends the next quarter." A formal system enforces this.
- **License revenue currently 3% of revenue; "we expect that to go north of that… It will go up soon."** Management will begin **reporting a Cogentiq revenue number every quarter from next quarter**, along with total license revenue.
- **Asper: "we expect the second half of fiscal year to be much stronger"** — ARR is already +59% YoY to $9 mn but Q1 revenue was flat because of the contract-to-revenue recognition lag.
- **Qure.ai: "a big jump from first half of the year to second half"** — backlog has risen to **INR 100+ cr from ~INR 20 cr** a year ago.
- **Profitability: "we expect that profitability will continue to improve over the next few quarters"** on a year-over-year basis; margins have now expanded for three consecutive quarters.
- **Europe growth (currently 25%) "can be meaningfully accelerated"** with a new Head of Europe being hired.
- **No revenue guidance for FY27.** On the year outlook, the CEO conceded: "our first quarter, we feel like we have certainly underachieved what we could have achieved… we hope that some of that will start to get addressed in the coming quarters."
- **CFO succession:** "we have made a ton of progress in identifying Ashwath's successor, and we will share more details once we have completed the full process."
order book & pipeline:
- **One of the largest single programs in Fractal's history won this quarter** — building AI foundations for a large healthcare player and modernising their data estate. Details promised "within a few days" of the call.
- **MoU signed in July with Mumbai's BMC** to pilot Vaidya.ai / Cogentiq Health across several public hospitals. Evaluation criteria: staff training, citizen feedback, doctor experience. A citywide rollout would become "a blueprint for other states and cities."
- **Cogentiq: early wins with more than 10 clients across industries**; AI-led transformation deals started with Cogentiq across CPG and financial services clients.
- **Partnerships are becoming deal gatekeepers** — "Partnerships decide who is even in the room for the biggest deals now." **Five of the largest deals this quarter came through a partner** (Databricks, OpenAI, Anthropic). 42 TTM joint engagements. Partnership-led revenue is still small in absolute terms — "a new muscle that we are building."
- **RFP dynamics changing:** "There are much larger RFPs coming through right now than we have seen in the past. The size of the deals are bigger and the ambition of what they want to get done are also much larger."
segment / subsidiary detail:
- **By vertical:** Healthcare & Life Sciences **+69% YoY** (now the second-largest vertical); Banking & Financial Services +36%; CPG & Retail (largest) +19%; **TMT −22%**. Ex-TMT growth was 35-37%.
- **By geography:** Europe +25%, Americas +24%, APAC & others −2% (hit by both TMT and the Middle East conflict).
- **Client metrics:** NPS 77 (from 73); **NRR 117% (from 108%)**; **0% churn**; new clients contributed 3% of growth. Clients >INR 20 mn TTM: 5 (from 4, but *down* from 6 sequentially — one TMT client slipped below); >INR 5 mn: 19 (from 18); **>INR 1 mn: 58 (from 54)**. Top-10 concentration **51.8%, down from 55.9%**. Must-Win Clients rose from 79% to **85%** of revenue.
- **Fractal Alpha (Asper + Analytics Vidhya):** like-for-like revenue +20% YoY; Analytics Vidhya +57% (+42% in dollar terms), Asper flat on revenue but ARR +59% to $9 mn, used by 20 CPG clients. Gross margin 65%; segment loss INR 14 cr (widened on the iqigai/EdTech transfer, not operations).
- **Qure.ai (associate):** revenue +160% YoY to INR 24 cr; backlog INR 100+ cr vs ~INR 20 cr; Fractal's share of loss INR 23 cr.
growth verticals / optionality:
- **Three-pronged go-to-market, newly organised:** **AIT** (AI-led business transformation — applications solving demand/supply/operations problems that drive client core metrics), **AIF** (AI Foundations — data foundations, ontology and knowledge layer, security, orchestration, application layers), **AIW** (AI for Work and Workforce re-imagination). A new Chief Commercial Officer (Matt) now owns go-to-market.
- **Cogentiq as the platform bet:** an enterprise platform that is model-agnostic ("They can use a multiple set of models") with vertical products built on top — **Cogentiq Underwriting** (insurance, "seeing a pretty solid traction"), **Cogentiq e-commerce**, and builds underway for supply chain and customer service. Top leaders have been assigned to each product. Revenue is **product-led**, possibly with an FDE/implementation component.
- **Cogentiq Health / Vaidya.ai** via the BMC pilot — a potential public-health distribution channel.
- **Leadership build-out** as the growth lever: new CCO, new Chief Practice Officer for BFS (Leandro), Head of Europe being hired, product leaders for each Cogentiq vertical.
6a. moat & competitive position:
- **Client economics are the moat:** 117% net revenue retention with **zero churn** and NPS 77 — clients expand, none leave. Only 3% of growth came from new clients, meaning virtually all growth is land-and-expand inside an installed base.
- **De-risking while deepening:** top-10 concentration fell 410 bps to 51.8% *while* the >INR 1 mn client count rose from 54 to 58 — growth is broadening, not concentrating.
- **Trust and control as the product thesis:** enterprises "want to make sure that their knowledge stays within the enterprise" and want to control outcomes "regardless of whether they have or lose model access" — Cogentiq's model-agnostic, enterprise-owned ontology layer is positioned exactly at that anxiety.
- **Foundation-model partnerships** (Databricks, OpenAI, Anthropic) now gate access to the largest deals; five of Fractal's largest deals this quarter came through a partner.
- Cybersecurity rated in the highest Black Kite category.
margins & cost dynamics: Gross margin expanded only 29 bps to 45.7% — a currency gain of 273 bps was almost entirely consumed by the merit increase (−75 bps) and a deliberate headcount build to support future growth (−169 bps). The real operating leverage is in SG&A, down from 26.2% to 24.3% of revenue, delivering the 189 bps adjusted EBITDA expansion. **Q2 carries a 120-130 bps P&L headwind** from three full months of merit increases versus one in Q1. ESOP charges including cash bonus and one-time retention fell to 1.2% of revenue from 1.4%. The margin philosophy is explicitly disciplined: R&D rises only as a share of *expanded* gross margin, enforced by a formal system, and the CEO is pushing R&D itself to "work backwards from revenue" for faster conversion. The mix shift toward outcome/output/license pricing (42% → target 60%) is the structural margin lever.
capex / expansion (watch slippage): Not a capex business; R&D is the equivalent. **INR 61 cr invested in Q1 (+31% YoY), of which INR 41 cr (4.5% of revenue) was expensed** — into Cogentiq, Asper and Analytics Vidhya. The trajectory is toward 10% of revenue, but explicitly gated on gross-margin expansion, so it self-throttles if margins stall. Headcount is being added ahead of revenue (a 169 bps gross-margin cost this quarter) — the visible investment slippage risk is if that build does not convert. Physical/organisational expansion is leadership hiring, with the Head of Europe still unfilled.
capital allocation: Balance sheet is deliberately clean post-IPO: **INR 1,639 cr of cash** including INR 689 cr of IPO proceeds, **long-term debt fully repaid in April 2026**, DSO improved to 71 days (54 billed), cash conversion to EBITDA ~70%, ROCE ~13%. Forward cover is taken only as a cash-flow hedge. Capital deployment priorities visible on the call: R&D into platforms (gated), senior leadership hiring, and continued funding of the Qure.ai associate position. No buyback, dividend or acquisition was discussed.
risks & watch-items:
- **TMT concentration risk realised.** A −22% YoY decline in one vertical cut group growth from 37% to 20%. The stated cause is structural, not idiosyncratic: big tech's AI capex "almost doubled," creating opex pressure and "big adjustments… in terms of how they look at the overall spends and allocating more of that to capex and less of that to opex." That pressure does not obviously reverse in a quarter.
- **The company has stopped disclosing client-specific issues** — "we have chosen to not talk about that in future because it is distracting." This reduces transparency exactly where the volatility is.
- **Currency dependence:** 11 of the 20 points of reported growth. cc revenue was *down* 0.4% sequentially.
- **CFO transition** at a moment when the equity story depends on financial credibility; successor unnamed.
- **AI work compression** — "anything that feels like it is not as relevant today… could be completely vanishing" (ad hoc analysis, dashboards "going to zero"). Management argues the expanding pie more than compensates, but the compression is certain and the compensation is a forecast.
- **Competitive intensity rising:** "there are also many players who want a piece of this pie right now… our execution has to really get better."
- Asper revenue flat despite 59% ARR growth — the recognition lag has to actually close in H2.
management quality / tone: Unusually accountable. The CEO refused to blame the TMT client — "I do not want to get into blaming anyone for our performance… I will take most of the blame on our own execution" — and repeatedly framed the shortfall as internal: "It is completely left to our execution to become as big as we can be. There is no other law of gravity applying to us." He conceded outright that "our quarter one is not as great as we would like it to be" and that Q1 "underachieved." Disclosure is improving voluntarily — committing to publish Cogentiq and license revenue from next quarter, and considering disclosing partnership-led revenue. The CFO gave precise bridges (currency vs merit vs headcount in gross margin; the exact Q2 merit impact) and corrected an analyst's mischaracterisation of the segment loss as a one-time integration cost. The one weakening of transparency is the deliberate policy to stop discussing client-specific issues.
non-obvious takeaways:
- **The reported 20% growth is really 9%.** Constant-currency revenue *fell* 0.4% sequentially. Every profitability metric is genuine; the top line is substantially FX.
- **The >INR 20 mn client count went 6 → 5 sequentially** even though it is up YoY (4 → 5) — a TMT client slipped below the threshold. Management guided investors to look at this annually, not on a TTM basis, which is a fair methodological point but also softens a negative datapoint.
- **The Fractal Alpha loss widening from INR 4 cr to INR 14 cr is an accounting relocation, not deterioration** — iqigai and EdTech investment simply moved segments, with FY26 restated. Reading it as operational decay is wrong.
- **AI deflation is being embraced as an expansion argument:** work that took a year may take a month, "which means that per se looks like it shrunk, but there are now 1,000 such deals rather than 10 such deals earlier." This is the central, unproven bet of the entire business model.
- Fractal is becoming a **partner-mediated** business — five of its largest deals came via Databricks/OpenAI/Anthropic — which is a new dependency it did not previously carry ("Most of our revenues used to come from direct client relationships").
- Qure.ai's backlog going from ~INR 20 cr to INR 100+ cr is arguably the largest forward-looking datapoint on the call, and it sits in an associate line most models treat as noise.

business_model.title: What they do
business_model.body: Fractal Analytics supports large global enterprises with data-driven insights and end-to-end AI solutions, working with clients across the entire life cycle of AI transformation from ideation to adoption, on the back of technical, domain and functional capabilities built over an operating history of more than 26 years. Its full suite of AI solutions is organized under two segments — Fractal.ai, comprising AI services and AI products primarily hosted on the Cogentiq platform, and Fractal Alpha, comprising AI businesses. Delivery is through integrated, client-facing business units organized by industry (Consumer Products and Retail, Financial Services and Insurance, Healthcare and Life Sciences, Technology Media and Telecom) and geography (APAC and Europe); Fractal.ai work is contracted under master service agreements with time-and-material, fixed-price and output-based pricing, while Fractal Alpha products are sold on licensing, subscription or fixed-price models with contracts typically running two to three years.

margins.title: Margins & cost dynamics
margins.body: Gross margin expanded only 29 bps to 45.7% — a currency gain of 273 bps was almost entirely consumed by the merit increase (−75 bps) and a deliberate headcount build to support future growth (−169 bps). The real operating leverage is in SG&A, down from 26.2% to 24.3% of revenue, delivering the 189 bps adjusted EBITDA expansion. **Q2 carries a 120-130 bps P&L headwind** from three full months of merit increases versus one in Q1. capex_expansion.title: Capex & expansion plans
capex_expansion.body: Fractal is an asset-light enterprise AI business, so its expansion narrative is about platform, capability, vertical and geographic build-out rather than plant or capacity addition. Cogentiq adoption is described as transitioning from POC to production deployment, with platform revenue expected to accelerate and drive further margin expansion in FY27. Capability build-out is funded by R&D: 6.4% of revenue was invested in R&D across the two segments in FY 2025-26, of which 4.1% was expensed and the balance capitalized on the back of intellectual property developed. Vertical and geographic expansion is evidenced by Healthcare & Life Sciences rising from 13.8% to 19.3% of revenue and Europe from 17.7% to 19.9%. Inorganic expansion is framed as optionality rather than a committed project: a strong cash position (stated as C20.5 billion) is said to enable disciplined inorganic growth through M&A to acquire complementary capabilities, verticals or geographies, while retaining flexibility for organic investment in R&D, talent and infrastructure. risks.title: Risks & watch-items
risks.body:
- **TMT concentration risk realised.** A −22% YoY decline in one vertical cut group growth from 37% to 20%. That pressure does not obviously reverse in a quarter.
- **The company has stopped disclosing client-specific issues** — "we have chosen to not talk about that in future because it is distracting." This reduces transparency exactly where the volatility is.
- **Currency dependence:** 11 of the 20 points of reported growth. cc revenue was *down* 0.4% sequentially.

non_obvious.title: Non-obvious takeaways
non_obvious.body:

- **The >INR 20 mn client count went 6 → 5 sequentially** even though it is up YoY (4 → 5) — a TMT client slipped below the threshold. Management guided investors to look at this annually, not on a TTM basis, which is a fair methodological point but also softens a negative datapoint.
- **The Fractal Alpha loss widening from INR 4 cr to INR 14 cr is an accounting relocation, not deterioration** — iqigai and EdTech investment simply moved segments, with FY26 restated. Reading it as operational decay is wrong.

capex / expansion (watch slippage): Not a capex business; R&D is the equivalent. **INR 61 cr invested in Q1 (+31% YoY), of which INR 41 cr (4.5% of revenue) was expensed** — into Cogentiq, Asper and Analytics Vidhya. The trajectory is toward 10% of revenue, but explicitly gated on gross-margin expansion, so it self-throttles if margins stall. Headcount is being added ahead of revenue (a 169 bps gross-margin cost this quarter) — the visible investment slippage risk is if that build does not convert. Physical/organisational expansion is leadership hiring, with the Head of Europe still unfilled.
capital allocation: Balance sheet is deliberately clean post-IPO: **INR 1,639 cr of cash** including INR 689 cr of IPO proceeds, **long-term debt fully repaid in April 2026**, DSO improved to 71 days (54 billed), cash conversion to EBITDA ~70%, ROCE ~13%. Forward cover is taken only as a cash-flow hedge. Capital deployment priorities visible on the call: R&D into platforms (gated), senior leadership hiring, and continued funding of the Qure.ai associate position. No buyback, dividend or acquisition was discussed.
risks & watch-items:
- **TMT concentration risk realised.** A −22% YoY decline in one vertical cut group growth from 37% to 20%. The stated cause is structural, not idiosyncratic: big tech's AI capex "almost doubled," creating opex pressure and "big adjustments… in terms of how they look at the overall spends and allocating more of that to capex and less of that to opex." That pressure does not obviously reverse in a quarter.
- **The company has stopped disclosing client-specific issues** — "we have chosen to not talk about that in future because it is distracting." This reduces transparency exactly where the volatility is.
- **Currency dependence:** 11 of the 20 points of reported growth. cc revenue was *down* 0.4% sequentially.
- **CFO transition** at a moment when the equity story depends on financial credibility; successor unnamed.
- **AI work compression** — "anything that feels like it is not as relevant today… could be completely vanishing" (ad hoc analysis, dashboards "going to zero"). Management argues the expanding pie more than compensates, but the compression is certain and the compensation is a forecast.
- **Competitive intensity rising:** "there are also many players who want a piece of this pie right now… our execution has to really get better."
- Asper revenue flat despite 59% ARR growth — the recognition lag has to actually close in H2.
management quality / tone: Unusually accountable. The CEO refused to blame the TMT client — "I do not want to get into blaming anyone for our performance… I will take most of the blame on our own execution" — and repeatedly framed the shortfall as internal: "It is completely left to our execution to become as big as we can be. There is no other law of gravity applying to us." He conceded outright that "our quarter one is not as great as we would like it to be" and that Q1 "underachieved." Disclosure is improving voluntarily — committing to publish Cogentiq and license revenue from next quarter, and considering disclosing partnership-led revenue. The CFO gave precise bridges (currency vs merit vs headcount in gross margin; the exact Q2 merit impact) and corrected an analyst's mischaracterisation of the segment loss as a one-time integration cost. The one weakening of transparency is the deliberate policy to stop discussing client-specific issues.
non-obvious takeaways:
- **The reported 20% growth is really 9%.** Constant-currency revenue *fell* 0.4% sequentially. Every profitability metric is genuine; the top line is substantially FX.
- **The >INR 20 mn client count went 6 → 5 sequentially** even though it is up YoY (4 → 5) — a TMT client slipped below the threshold. Management guided investors to look at this annually, not on a TTM basis, which is a fair methodological point but also softens a negative datapoint.
- **The Fractal Alpha loss widening from INR 4 cr to INR 14 cr is an accounting relocation, not deterioration** — iqigai and EdTech investment simply moved segments, with FY26 restated. Reading it as operational decay is wrong.
- **AI deflation is being embraced as an expansion argument:** work that took a year may take a month, "which means that per se looks like it shrunk, but there are now 1,000 such deals rather than 10 such deals earlier." This is the central, unproven bet of the entire business model.
- Fractal is becoming a **partner-mediated** business — five of its largest deals came via Databricks/OpenAI/Anthropic — which is a new dependency it did not previously carry ("Most of our revenues used to come from direct client relationships").
- Qure.ai's backlog going from ~INR 20 cr to INR 100+ cr is arguably the largest forward-looking datapoint on the call, and it sits in an associate line most models treat as noise.
